resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndLocation reads 'Exter' (an evident typo, presumably meaning Exeter, NH), and independent sources genuinely split on which Seacoast-area town the pipeline actually terminated at. FOUR independent sources -- including the sponsor's own primary disclosure -- name STRATHAM as the Seacoast-end interconnect: (1) Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp's own SEC Form 40-F FY2017 AIF: 'the proposed Granite Bridge project would connect the existing Portland Natural Gas Transmission System and Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline facilities in Stratham with the existing Tennessee Gas Pipeline facilities in Manchester'; (2) NHPR: 'run about 27 miles along Route 101 between Stratham and Manchester'; (3) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' (rev. 7/18): 'Location: Manchester, NH - Stratham, NH'; (4) InDepthNH (31 Jul 2020): '16-inch-wide steel underground pipeline that would run 27 miles, from Stratham to Manchester.' TWO independent sources instead name EXETER: Seacoastonline (17 Mar 2019): 'The proposed underground 27-mile, 16-inch diameter pipeline from Manchester to Exeter,' plus detail that Liberty held an easement with the TOWN of Exeter to build a metering station there; and the Union Leader (1 Aug 2020): 'would have followed Route 101 to bring natural gas from Exeter to Manchester.' Reading Seacoastonline closely resolves part of the puzzle without fully closing it: the Select Board minutes it cites say that had Exeter rejected the metering-station easement, 'Liberty would've been forced to build its metering station in Stratham' -- i.e. Stratham was the fallback site for a METERING STATION along the route, while the pipeline's actual upstream interconnect with PNGTS/M&NE (per Liberty's own SEC filing) was in Stratham. It is plausible the two press accounts naming Exeter are describing the metering-station host town rather than the pipeline's true end-of-line interconnect, but I could not find a single source stating both facts explicitly enough to settle it with certainty. Given the sponsor's own regulatory filing plus three more independent accounts say Stratham, EndLocation is more likely Stratham than Exeter; flagging as a spec/attribution concern rather than silently overwriting, since two independent regional papers do say Exeter. StartLocation=Manchester is undisputed across every source.

(4) February 2022 -- MDN reports Talen actively working on the Montour coal-to-gas conversion (MDN 2022/02 article). Four independent, verified sources converge on the opposite conclusion -- this lateral was built and put into service, not cancelled: (1) The Oklahoman, Dec 14 2016 (reporting Enable's own announcement): Enable Midstream Partners LP signed a 20-year, 228,000 Dth/d gas supply contract with OG&E on the Enable Oklahoma Intrastate Transmission (EOIT) system, to build 77 miles of 20-inch pipe to OG&E's Muskogee plant, contract to start 2018. (3) OGE Energy Corp SEC 10-K for FY2018 (filed 2019-02-21, verified live): 'OG&E has invested $50.5 million in the Muskogee natural gas conversion' as of Dec 31 2018, describing the project as actively 'converting.' (4) OGE Energy Corp SEC 10-K for FY2019 (filed 2020-02-27, verified live): states plainly 'OG&E converted two coal-fired generating units at the Muskogee Station to natural gas' and 'Muskogee Units 4 and 5 were placed into service in March 2019' -- and the FY2019 unit-by-unit generating-capability table lists Muskogee Units 4 and 5 as 'Steam-Turbine Gas' (changed from 'Steam-Turbine Coal' in the same table in the FY2018 10-K). Three distinct origins (a newspaper covering Enable's announcement, an independent trade-press project tracker, and OG&E's own audited SEC disclosures) all point the same direction: the fuel-supply lateral this row represents was completed, which is *why* two 500 MW coal units could switch to gas -- a cancelled, never-built pipeline could not produce that outcome. resolutions.researcher_notes: MAJOR FINDING -- this is not a cancelled project, it was built. Kinder Morgan's Texas Intrastate Pipelines group signed a 20-year firm transportation agreement with SK E&S LNG, LLC in December 2014 to invest >$150M and build ~40 miles of pipe from its Tejas mainline to an interconnect with Freeport LNG's existing pipeline at Stratton Ridge, TX, to support Freeport LNG Train III (LNG World News, 2014-12-09, Wayback capture -- name_found on 'SK LNG'). Kinder Morgan's own SEC 8-K exhibit filed 2015-01-21 restates the identical $150M/320,000 Dth/d/Quintana Island/Train III facts (name_found on 'SK E&S'). This is exactly the project the sheet calls 'SK Pipeline' -- SK is the counterparty's name. I then traced KMI's disclosures forward year by year and found CONTINUOUS, UNBROKEN progress with no mention of suspension or cancellation at any point: the Q2/Q3 2016 8-Ks describe it as 'Phase 2' of a combined 'Texas Intrastate Crossover' project (est. cost $161M then $326M total both phases) 'supported by a long-term commitment from SK E&S LNG, LLC ... to service the Freeport LNG export facility,' expected in service late 2018; the FY2016 10-K (filed 2017-02-10) still shows it active, now targeting 3Q2019, same SK E&S language; the FY2017 10-K (filed 2018-02-09) unchanged; the FY2018 10-K (filed 2019-02-08) shows Phase 2 slipped to 2Q2020 at $298M; and the FY2019 10-K (filed 2020-02-12) states plainly 'Phase 1 and Phase 2 are in service' at a final $288M. A contemporaneous, independent trade-press snapshot mid-stream -- Pipeline & Gas Journal's 'Ongoing Projects' list, October 2018 issue (PN1018-Ongoing-Projects.pdf, verified name_found='SK Pipeline' literally) -- lists 'SK Pipeline' by that exact name under Kinder Morgan Inc., 30-inch diameter, West Columbia TX-Stratton Ridge TX, 320 MDth/d, completion 3Q2019, 'to support Train III export capacity as part of the Freeport LNG Export Project' -- pinning the PGJ project-list entry to the identical SK E&S commitment tracked in KMI's own filings. GEM's ShelvedYear=2016 and CancelledYear=2018 (ShelvedCancelledType=inferred, i.e. GUESSED from apparent dormancy after the initial 2014 press coverage went quiet) are contradicted by every one of these filings -- the project was never dormant, it was mid-construction the whole time, and it was completed. Recommend Status->operating and clearing the Shelved/Cancelled fields entirely (see status_reviews for the full proposed edit and Shelved/Cancelled [ref] fills below for why those units are UNRESOLVED rather than re-sourced). CAVEAT on precision: none of my sources independently confirm that the FINAL as-built pipe segment retained the exact original 40-mile/30-inch West Columbia-Stratton Ridge alignment once it was folded into the larger, multi-shipper 'Texas Intrastate Crossover Expansion' (which also serves Cheniere Corpus Christi LNG and CFE/Mexico from the Katy Hub) -- KMI's disclosures track the SK E&S COMMERCIAL COMMITMENT continuously to completion, not a discrete as-built map of this specific lateral. I searched SEC full-text search for 'Kinder Morgan' + 'Stratton Ridge' for a second, non-KMI confirmation of completion and found only unrelated pre-2011 filings about KMI's separate Stratton Ridge gas STORAGE facility; WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) so I could not chase a Freeport LNG-side or FERC/RRC confirmation of the exact built route. The status-change evidence itself is therefore single-origin (Kinder Morgan's own SEC filings, tier=medium per the independence rule) even though it is unusually strong (five consecutive annual/quarterly SEC filings over 2014-2020, unbroken).

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE AND CLASSIFICATION: the underlying pipe is real, FERC-certificated, gas transmission infrastructure -- not in question. What is wrong is treating it as cancelled. GEM's own dates (ShelvedYear=2010, CancelledYear=2012) line up almost exactly with real FERC milestones for TEAM 2012 (PF10-21 pre-filing NOI published 2010-08-26, 75 FR 52524; formal application 2011-02-11, FERC Docket CP11-67-000; amended 2011-06-30; EA notice 2011-09-02, 36-inch pipe through Greene/Fayette/Franklin/Adams/Fulton Counties PA plus a Bedford Compressor Station upgrade in Bedford County PA) -- but instead of ending in cancellation, a FERC 'Combined Notice of Filings' dated 2012-09-12 (77 FR, Docket CP11-67) records Texas Eastern's own 'TEAM 2012 In-Service Filing -- CP11-67 Compliance to be effective 11/1/2012.' The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', row 731) independently corroborates this from a completely different agency/dataset: 'TETCO TEAM 2012 Expansion' / Texas Eastern Transmission / Status=Completed / Completed Date 2012-10-31 / Docket CP11-67. Two independent government sources (FERC's own docket record and EIA's separately-compiled tracking dataset) agree this project reached commercial service, not cancellation, in late 2012 -- squarely on top of GEM's recorded CancelledYear. Texas Eastern did not stop there: a second FERC pre-filing (PF12-19, NOI 2012-10-15, 77 FR 62507) opened for the 'Texas Eastern and Appalachia Market Expansion Project 2014 (TEAM 2014)' -- construction/modification in PA/WV/OH/KY/TN/AL/MS -- which became Docket CP13-84 (application 2013-03-21; EA notice 2013-09-23) and, per EIA workbook row 785, also reached 'Completed' status with an in-service date of 2014-11-07. This is a textbook case of the pattern this sweep was told to test for: a project shelved/re-scoped under FERC review is not cancelled if it is later built under the docket's actual project name. GEM's row 'TEMAX Pipeline Expansion' appears to be an informal/garbled label for this TEAM program rather than a name FERC or any source actually used (searched: no FERC docket, EIA row, or press hit for the literal string 'TEMAX'). DUPLICATE CHECK: neither 'TEAM 2012'/CP11-67 nor 'TEAM 2014'/CP13-84 appears as a named pipeline/segment in the 45-row US-gas cohort roster provided for this batch, so I cannot confirm from the material given to me whether either successor is ALREADY tracked as a separate GEM PID elsewhere in the full 131-column Gas tab (outside this batch's scope).
